title: The Spear Hero's Sniper Shot
paragraphs: “I am well aware that the demands from Schildwelt kept you awake night after night. As for what Siltvelt thinks of Shieldfreeden… well, while it recognizes them as victims exploited by the Takt faction—led by Nelshen, who served as your country’s representative—it’s also fair to say that the Takt faction’s influence still runs deep. To bring about that reform, I’d like to introduce the figure your country desires—the one I’ve been lacking—right here.”
As Father spoke, Rival materialized and gradually began to transform.
“GRAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!”
Rival transforms while letting out an incredibly loud roar. It’s quite a sight, considering he usually changes form effortlessly, as if it were child’s play.

Eventually, he took on the form of a dragon—a design practiced in Siltvelt, featuring a white, divine appearance with red accents. The wings seem to incorporate a slightly bird-like design. That’s a privilege reserved for Filolial-sama! And what’s with the four wings, I ask? Using Magic to create a dramatic effect where light streams down from the sky—that’s way too over-the-top!
“Oh…”
I can hear the audience letting out gasps of admiration. Are they really being fooled by something this trivial? What a gullible bunch they are. Don’t let yourselves be fooled, everyone!

“I have come here in response to the call of the Shield Hero. My name is Gaelion. I have descended upon Shieldfreeden to atone for the sins committed by my foolish kin. I command the people of Shieldfreeden: The time has come to awaken from the curse of the Evil Dragon, who once served under Takt—that foolish, false hero!”
Rival spoke in a deep voice that echoed far and wide, seizing the moment. Then, sparks flew around Rival’s face.

I can see it, you know. There were guys sniping at him from a distance with firearms, trying to intercept Rival as he soared high through the air. Father looked slightly concerned, but Rival waved his hand, as if to say everything was fine.
“Don’t be ridiculous! None of us in Shieldfreeden would ever be deceived by a false god!”

I could hear such voices mingling among the crowd. Even for me, it’d be a real pain to pick out the guy who said that from the crowd. Is it around there? Well, I’m not going to step forward just because Rival got sniped. But if Father were the target, I’d destroy him on the spot.
“...Foolish. It seems I have no choice but to demonstrate my power. I’ll give you five seconds. If you beg for your life right now, I might just spare you.”

It feels off without that trademark drawl and flippant tone. The only image I can picture of you is fawning over Father—and inevitably failing. For the next five seconds or so, I heard gunshots ringing out repeatedly.
“I can’t have you underestimating my strength… From my perspective, even an attack from that ‘Spear Hero’ who startled you lot is a piece of cake.”
What did you say?! You said that! Well, then, I’ll show you! I’ll throw an Air Strike Javelin at you, disguised as a bullet. I shrank my spear down to the size of a toothpick before saying,
“Air Strike Javelin!”
“Wait—”
“Lame.”

Damn… Rival knocked it right out of the sky. The reason I lost was that disguising it prevented it from unleashing its full power. If I’d attacked in earnest, a rival like that would be nothing more than a pushover.
“Sigh… How lamentable. That those who worship such an evil dragon and a false hero are running rampant to this extent… And do you understand now? Even the Spear Hero cannot threaten me.”
I felt like all eyes were on me.
Are you trying to use me as a stepping stone?! I’ll unleash Brionac on you!
Just as I was about to say that, I sensed Father giving me a warning look, so I held back. Damn youuuuuuu… you Rival!
“Then, die!”
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa――!?”

When Rival snapped his fingers, the culprit in the audience and the sniper firing from afar both seemed to burst into flames. By the way, that “five-second grace period” is probably just the time the sniper needs to take aim. So there was never any grace period to begin with. Me? Haha, there’s no way I’d burst into flames from Magic this weak.
“Aaaaaaah!?”
“Ooooh!?”

Of course, since the guy who’d been firing his gun nonstop was in the center of the expanding circle, he was an easy target—but the sudden burst of flames seems to have thrown the surrounding audience into total chaos. Haha, it’s just Rival’s speech, after all. A total failure.
“Calm downnnnnnnnnnnnnn!”

At Rival’s roar, the crowd—already in utter chaos—fell into a state of panic and froze in place. A wide-area binding Magic spell, I see. Sure, it managed to quell the physical chaos, but is this really for the best?
“What’s there to hesitate about? I’ve merely selected and judged those who worship a false god. They… have simply pulled the trigger themselves.”
It’s only natural that they get what they deserve. That just shows how much Father and Rival are in their way. I, too, find Rival’s presence a major nuisance.

“From now on, I will help Takt, Nelshen, and the people move away from the false freedom incited by the evil dragon Leirdia, and toward the true freedom that Shieldfreeden stands for from its very inception. “My fellow citizens… let us join forces and bring about a rebirth of our nation!”

The moment Rival declared this in a loud voice, the state of panic lifted, and sparse applause could be heard from among the citizens, who were staring up in astonishment. Gradually, the sound of the applause grew louder, and cheers erupted.
Ugh… I’m extremely dissatisfied, but it seems Rival’s speech was a success. Soon, Rival shifted form, landed in human form, and stood beside Father.

“Well then, people of Shieldfreeden, I look forward to working with you from now on. Not only will I eliminate the nation’s debt, but I also intend to fulfill my role as a hero by properly dealing with the waves… If you try to interfere, I think you’ve seen from this incident what will happen.”

Father added a slightly menacing edge to his voice at the end, then stepped down from the podium with Rival and returned to his seat. A murmur rose from the crowd—a sound that could be interpreted as confusion, couldn’t it? Paying no heed to it, we returned inside the building once more.
“Well then, Motoyasu-kun?”

Father, wearing a smile that carried a spine-chilling aura, approached me. This aura—different from Father in the first world—is sending chills down my spine. What does it remind me of…? Ah, I don’t know—it reminds me of the killing intent of that pig who stabbed me, and it’s terrifying. It’s similar to when Kou grinned and said he was going to eat Keel and Mole.
“W-What is it!?”
“You attacked by hiding among the bullets just because Gaelion-chan provoked you, didn’t you? I saw everything.”
Gulp!? Just as I thought, Father saw me. Should I try to cover this up? No, I swore to Filo-chan that I’d live honestly, so I’ll tell the truth.
“I just returned the blow. Rival is the one at fault.”
“Well, he provoked me, saying, ‘I bet the Spear Hero would do it.’ Now they’ll have to wonder if they should worship Gaelion—who can even drive back the Spear Hero, whom they considered a threat.”
Rival seizes the moment and says this with a sigh. I won’t forgive him for using me as a stepping stone!
“What were you planning to do if Motoyasu-kun had attacked you with everything he had, without taking his eyes off you?”
“I’d trained enough to be able to dodge it.”
“Don’t get too cocky! Father, if I’d gone all out, Rival would be nothing but a pile of ashes by now!”
“I understand how you feel, but if he’d been reduced to ashes in that situation, it would’ve been a real problem…”
“The bad blood between Dragons and Filolials runs deep, doesn’t it?”
“Of course, there’s no doubt that Lord Kitamura’s actions were barbaric.”
Even the panda and Eclair are being incited! I’m not the bad guy here! I didn’t use enough force to kill anyone. It’s just a bit of harassment—no more than a pea shooter, really.
“Rival is trying to frame me. Father, this is a conspiracy!”
“Yeah, yeah. Motoyasu, try to act your age, okay? And Gaelion, please don’t go provoking Motoyasu on the fly…”
“As long as the result’s okay, it’s fine!”
What do you mean, “as long as the result’s okay”?! Because of you, my position is in jeopardy!
“I wonder if this is really going to be okay… I’m getting even more anxious now.”
“It’ll be fine.”
“I can fully understand your anxiety, Lord Iwatani.”
“It really makes you worry about what’s to come, doesn’t it?”
“Ugh… I feel the same way as everyone else.”
All three Knights shared their thoughts on Rival’s speech. Ha ha! After all, that’s all Rival is worth! It’s practically their job to stoke everyone’s anxiety.
“By the way, Spear Hero,”
“What is it?”
“To cement Gaelion’s charisma, you need to mass-produce the bio-plant seeds you already have and send them over. Food, clothing, and shelter come first.”
Ugh… He’s just barging right into my achievements without a second thought. I’ve got to firmly assert my rights here. Otherwise, I’ll end up like Itsuki.
“This is the achievement of me, Father, and Filolial-sama!”
“Oh, for heaven’s sake…”
“I suppose this is what they mean by ‘talking yourself into a corner.’”
“If you’ve got something that revolutionary, shouldn’t you just hand it over already?”
“Yes. I believe that would be for the good of the world, Spear Hero.”
“Motoyasu, is that okay with you?”

Since Father is holding out his hand, I’ll reluctantly hand it over. I’ve already obtained and modified it, but I’m not happy about this. I was planning to give it to Father later, when the need arose. After all, depending on how it’s used, it could become a dangerous item.
“Is this… the plant seed Motoyasu-kun mentioned when we were leveling up—the one I used for reform in the future?”
“That’s right! I retrieved it and modified it before my blunder happened! Let’s use this to show Father’s prestige to the whole world! ”

“Well, what we need to do right now is rebuild Shieldfreeden while rooting out the Takt faction… That said, even though we’ll ultimately credit Motoyasu-kun as the first discoverer, it seems we’d get more public support if we let the world think Gaelion-chan provided them.”
Is even Father saying things like that? Why on earth do we have to give the credit to some dragon? To hell with rationality!
“Exactly! We should reveal what the Spear Hero actually did once the results are in, but for now, we have to hold back.”
“Grrr… I’ll remember this!”

So, it seems I handed Father a mass-produced batch of Bio-Plant seeds, and Rival will be traveling around various parts of Shieldfreeden giving speeches while carrying those seeds. As for Father, while he occasionally gives speeches alongside Rival as part of his official duties, the rest of the time he seems to be over in Siltvelt via the portal.
It’s going according to plan, but it’s still a bit surprising. It’s eerie to see that Rival not clinging to Father’s heels. No matter what anyone says, it seems we need to stay on our guard.
Don’t let anyone fool you!

As originally planned, I began my missionary work to spread the word of Filolial-sama in Shieldfreeden. Ah, as for the disturbances occurring around the world, they’re such trivial matters that there’s no need to even report them. For the most part, they were immediately quelled through the combined efforts of myself, Father, Éclair, and the others, with Filolial-sama’s cooperation.

Some time later. It seems a room was prepared for Rival at Shieldfreeden Castle, and a mountain of paperwork began piling up there. When I went to check on the situation with Father, Rival was organizing the documents.

By the way, thanks to the bio-plant seeds I gave Rival, it seems the food shortage in Shieldfreeden is starting to improve. As a result, it seems his approval ratings have been rising now that people no longer have to worry about going hungry.
“Wow… that’s a mountain of paperwork.”
“Yeah… it keeps coming in day after day—I can’t believe they actually manage to keep up with it.”
It seems Rival’s voice has lost a bit of its vigor. Oh? The councilor who proposed the dragon to Father is mingling among the paperwork, acting as if he were an aide.
“His Dragon Highness is reaching conclusions every day without sleeping.”
“Without sleeping!? Gaelion-chan, are you okay!?”
“This is nothing. If a dragon puts its mind to it, it can fight for years without sleeping…”
“Wait, aren’t you tired?”
“I’m fine. I’m doing all this for Naofumi.”
“Gaelion-chan…”
I get the feeling there’s some kind of strange tension hanging in the air between Rival and Father. Rival’s gaze is fixed on the paperwork, so he doesn’t seem to have noticed.
“The expenses here are off. Look into it. If anyone looks like they’re lining their own pockets under the guise of ‘humanity,’ deal with them immediately.”
“Yes. How should we handle this issue?”

“This one’s working too hard. If we don’t give them a break, they won’t last. It’s all about keeping them alive but not overworking them—that’s how you ensure a healthy, sustainable workflow. Or rather… the legacy of the previous leader has become toxic in so many ways that the whole system is falling apart.”
“I’m at a loss for words…”
The council member assisting her is apologizing. Well, it seems he’s doing what he’s supposed to. Just keep working like a slave, that’s the order.
“Gaelion-chan, are you really okay?”
“I told you, I’m fine. Since Gaelion can also use the power of a Demon Lord from another world, I’m having the monsters I’ve subjugated shoulder my fatigue, so I don’t get that tired.”
“Doing something like that… when did you…?”
“I made them my subordinates through a little serendipity while touring various parts of Shieldfreeden for my speeches. It’s the descent of the Demon King Gaelion, after all.”
“No, are you really okay? In every sense of the word?”
Just as she said that, Rival was looking over some documents while cracking his neck.
